questions.stem:
In the following reactions, P, Q, R, and S are the major products.
(CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl —(i) Mg, dry ether (ii) H₂O→ P
(CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl —(i) Mg, dry ether (ii) CO₂, dry ether (iii) H₃O⁺ (iv) NaOH→ Q
(CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl —(i) Mg, dry ether (ii) CH₃CHO, then H₂O (iii) CrO₃→ R
(CH₃)₂CHCH₂Cl —(i) ethanolic NaCN (ii) H₂/Ni (iii) CHCl₃/KOH, Δ (iv) LiAlH₄, then H₂O→ S
The correct statement about P, Q, R, and S is

options.text: P is a primary alcohol with four carbons.
Q undergoes Kolbe’s electrolysis to give an eight-carbon product.
R has six carbons and it undergoes Cannizzaro reaction.
S is a primary amine with six carbons.

questions.solution: P: the Grignard reagent is protonated by water, giving isobutane, an alkane, not an alcohol. Q: carboxylation gives 3-methylbutanoic acid, and NaOH turns it into its sodium salt; Kolbe electrolysis couples two (CH₃)₂CHCH₂• radicals into 2,5-dimethylhexane, an eight-carbon product, so (B) is true. R: addition to CH₃CHO gives 4-methylpentan-2-ol, and CrO₃ oxidises it to 4-methylpentan-2-one, a ketone with α-H that cannot undergo Cannizzaro. S: (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CN → (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₂NH₂ → isocyanide (carbylamine) → LiAlH₄ reduces –NC to –NHCH₃, giving a secondary amine.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem: A disaccharide X cannot be oxidised by bromine water. The acid hydrolysis of X leads to a laevorotatory solution. The disaccharide X is
questions.solution: Not being oxidised by bromine water means X has no free hemiacetal (it is a non-reducing sugar), so both anomeric carbons are tied up in the glycosidic bond. A laevorotatory hydrolysate (invert sugar) points to sucrose, whose hydrolysis gives D-glucose (+52.5°) and D-fructose (−92.4°). Option (A) is α-D-glucopyranosyl-(1→2)-β-D-fructofuranoside, which is sucrose. Options (B) and (C) keep a free anomeric OH on the glucose unit, so they are reducing, and (D) is a glucose–glucose 1→1 dimer whose hydrolysate is not laevorotatory.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
In the following reactions, P, Q, R, and S are the major products (structures 1–4 are the starting materials, in order).
1 —(i) KMnO₄, KOH, Δ (ii) H₃O⁺→ P
2 —(i) NaOH, H₂O (ii) H₃O⁺→ Q
3 —(i) H₃O⁺, Δ (ii) H₂CrO₄→ R
4 —(i) Mg, dry ether (ii) CO₂, then H₃O⁺ (iii) Ammoniacal AgNO₃, H₃O⁺→ S
The correct statement(s) about P, Q, R, and S is(are)

options.text: P and Q are monomers of polymers dacron and glyptal, respectively.
P, Q, and R are dicarboxylic acids.
Compounds Q and R are the same.
R does not undergo aldol condensation and S does not undergo Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.solution: P: hot alkaline KMnO₄ oxidises the ethyl group (it has benzylic H) to COOH but leaves the tert-butyl group alone, giving 4-tert-butylbenzoic acid, a monocarboxylic acid. Q: both the ester and the acid chloride are hydrolysed, giving isophthalic acid (benzene-1,3-dicarboxylic acid). R: acid hydrolyses the nitrile and the ester, the β-keto acid decarboxylates to 3-acetylbenzoic acid, and chromic acid oxidises the methyl ketone to COOH, again isophthalic acid, so Q = R. S: the Grignard reagent is carboxylated and the acid workup frees the aldehyde from the acetal; Tollens' reagent then oxidises CHO to COOH, giving terephthalic acid. Isophthalic acid has no α-H (no aldol) and terephthalic acid has no CHO (no Cannizzaro), so (D) holds. P is not a Dacron monomer and is not a diacid, so (A) and (B) fail.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.stem:
The reaction of 4-methyloct-1-ene (P, 2.52 g) with HBr in the presence of (C₆H₅CO)₂O₂ gives two isomeric bromides in a 9 : 1 ratio, with a combined yield of 50%. Of these, the entire amount of the primary alkyl bromide was reacted with an appropriate amount of diethylamine followed by treatment with aq. K₂CO₃ to give a non-ionic product S in 100% yield.
The mass (in mg) of S obtained is ___.
[Use molar mass (in g mol⁻¹): H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, Br = 80]
questions.solution: P is C₉H₁₈ (M = 126), so 2.52 g = 0.020 mol. With peroxide, HBr adds anti-Markovnikov, so the major (9 parts) bromide is the primary 1-bromo-4-methyloctane. The combined yield is 50%, i.e. 0.010 mol of bromides, of which 0.009 mol is primary. Diethylamine gives the tertiary ammonium salt, and K₂CO₃ frees the neutral amine C₉H₁₉N(C₂H₅)₂ = C₁₃H₂₉N (M = 199). Mass of S = 0.009 × 199 g = 1.791 g = 1791 mg.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.passage:
A trinitro compound, 1,3,5-tris-(4-nitrophenyl)benzene, on complete reaction with an excess of Sn/HCl gives a major product, which on treatment with an excess of NaNO₂/HCl at 0 °C provides P as the product. P, upon treatment with excess of H₂O at room temperature, gives the product Q. Bromination of Q in aqueous medium furnishes the product R. The compound P upon treatment with an excess of phenol under basic conditions gives the product S.
The molar mass difference between compounds Q and R is 474 g mol⁻¹ and between compounds P and S is 172.5 g mol⁻¹.
questions.stem:
The number of heteroatoms present in one molecule of R is ______ .
[Use: Molar mass (in g mol⁻¹): H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Br = 80, Cl = 35.5. Atoms other than C and H are considered as heteroatoms]
questions.solution: Sn/HCl reduces the three NO₂ groups to NH₂, and diazotisation gives the tris(diazonium) chloride P. Warming with water replaces each N₂⁺ by OH, giving Q, 1,3,5-tris(4-hydroxyphenyl)benzene. Each Br substituting an H adds 80 − 1 = 79 g mol⁻¹, and 474/79 = 6, so R carries six Br (two ortho to each OH; the para positions are blocked). R therefore has 3 O + 6 Br = 9 heteroatoms.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper

questions.passage:
A trinitro compound, 1,3,5-tris-(4-nitrophenyl)benzene, on complete reaction with an excess of Sn/HCl gives a major product, which on treatment with an excess of NaNO₂/HCl at 0 °C provides P as the product. P, upon treatment with excess of H₂O at room temperature, gives the product Q. Bromination of Q in aqueous medium furnishes the product R. The compound P upon treatment with an excess of phenol under basic conditions gives the product S.
The molar mass difference between compounds Q and R is 474 g mol⁻¹ and between compounds P and S is 172.5 g mol⁻¹.
questions.stem:
The total number of carbon atoms and heteroatoms present in one molecule of S is ______ .
[Use: Molar mass (in g mol⁻¹): H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Br = 80, Cl = 35.5. Atoms other than C and H are considered as heteroatoms]
questions.solution: P is the tris(diazonium chloride). Coupling with phenol in base replaces each –N₂⁺Cl⁻ by –N=N–C₆H₄OH (para), which adds 93 − 35.5 = 57.5 g mol⁻¹ per site. 3 × 57.5 = 172.5 matches the given difference, so all three sites couple. S = 1,3,5-tris[4-(4-hydroxyphenylazo)phenyl]benzene: C = 6 + 3×6 + 3×6 = 42, N = 6, O = 3, total 42 + 9 = 51.

check.note: Two independent solutions agree; the official key is not in the archived paper
